pdf_explanation: The figure on the left, composed of all the three elements, rotates by 90° clockwise around the centre of the whole group to give the figure on the right side.
why: From figure 1 to figure 2, the whole group of three shapes turns 90° clockwise as one piece, so every shape moves to a new place and turns too. Turning figure 3 the same way puts the star at the top right with its black half on top, the pentagon on the left pointing right, and the rounded box at the bottom right standing up with its white strip at the bottom. That is option 3. Option 2 is tempting, but its rounded box sits at the top and its white strip is on the wrong side.
trick: Treat the whole group as one picture and turn it: check both where each shape goes and which side its shading ends up on.
note: PDF answer C checked: it is the 90° clockwise rotation of figure 3. Option 5 is figure 3 unchanged; options 1, 2 and 4 have shapes in the wrong places or turned the wrong way.
